Biomass (corn cob) derived porous carbon with a very high surface area for supercapacitor application is reported by carbonization with a non-toxic mixed salt of NaCl and KCl as the reaction medium. The corn cob was subjected to molten salt carbonization in a molten NaCl-KCl system (mass ratio of 1 : 5) at 800 °C, porous carbon material (C-1-5) with a high specific surface area (1054.36 m2 g−1) and a three-dimensional honeycomb network structure was obtained. The electrode material exhibits a specific capacitance of 222.5 F g−1 in a three-electrode system at a current density of 0.1 A g−1. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor achieves a specific capacitance of 76.47 F g−1 at a scan rate of 5 mV s−1. The energy density is 6.22 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 50 W kg−1, and the capacitance retention reaches 96.30 % after 2000 cycles. This green and simple technology is expected to become an effective and scalable method for producing porous carbon from biomass for electrochemical energy storage applications.
